author: Robert Carr
description: A fragrant red curry soup with browned chicken, mushrooms, edamame and vegetables in a light coconut broth. Ginger, lime, scallions and basil keep it vivid rather than heavy or bland.
equipment: 8-quart Dutch oven or heavy soup pot

ingredients: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) unbrined boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
12 oz (340 g) frozen unsalted shelled edamame, not pods
2 tbsp (27 g) canola oil, divided into 1 tsp, 1 tsp, 2 tsp and 2 tsp portions
10 oz (283 g) cremini mushrooms, cleaned, dried and sliced
1 medium yellow onion (200 g peeled), thinly sliced
3 medium carrots (250 g trimmed), thinly sliced into 1/8-inch half-moons
1 large red bell pepper (200 g trimmed), cut into thin strips
2 tbsp (25 g) finely grated fresh ginger
4 tbsp (60 g) mild Thai red curry paste, with 400 mg sodium or less per tbsp; see brand/heat note
1 can (13.5 fl oz / 400 mL) light coconut milk, shaken, divided into 1/2 cup (120 mL) and 280 mL
4 cups (960 mL) low-sodium chicken broth, with 70 mg sodium or less per cup
1 tbsp (15 mL) reduced-sodium soy sauce, with 600 mg sodium or less per tbsp
1 bunch scallions (60 g trimmed), sliced and divided into 30 g white/light-green parts and 30 g dark-green parts
1/2 cup (16 g) chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems
1/2 cup (12 g) Thai basil leaves, torn; ordinary basil may be substituted
instructions: Pat 1 1/2 lb (680 g) chicken pieces dry. Heat 1 tsp (4.5 g) canola oil in an 8-quart pot over medium-high heat. Add 340 g chicken in a single layer and brown for 3 minutes without moving, then turn and cook for 1 minute. Transfer to a bowl. Heat 1 tsp (4.5 g) canola oil and repeat with the second 340 g chicken, cooking for 3 minutes on the first side and 1 minute on the second. Transfer to the bowl and continue immediately; the chicken is not fully cooked yet.

Add 2 tsp (9 g) canola oil and 10 oz (283 g) sliced mushrooms to the pot. Cook for 7-9 minutes, stirring occasionally, until their liquid has evaporated and their edges are brown. Reduce the heat if the coating on the pot threatens to burn.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add 2 tsp (9 g) canola oil, 1 sliced onion (200 g), 3 thinly sliced carrots (250 g), 1 sliced red bell pepper (200 g), and 30 g scallion white/light-green parts. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the onion softens. Add 6 minced garlic cloves (20 g) and 2 tbsp (25 g) ginger; stir for 30 seconds.

Add 4 tbsp (60 g) mild red curry paste and stir for 45-60 seconds until fragrant, without scorching it. Pour in 1/2 cup (120 mL) shaken light coconut milk. Scrape up the brown coating and simmer for 2 minutes, stirring, to combine the coconut milk and curry paste. Light coconut milk does not need to split or release oil for this step to work.

Add 280 mL light coconut milk and 4 cups (960 mL) chicken broth. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add 12 oz (340 g) frozen shelled edamame and all browned chicken from the 680 g raw batch with its collected juices. Simmer gently for 6 minutes, then stir in 6 oz (170 g) baby spinach and cook for 2-4 minutes. Check several of the largest chicken pieces reach 165 F (74 C), the edamame is fully cooked according to its package directions, and the carrots are tender. Remove chicken pieces as they reach temperature if the vegetables need longer.

Turn off the heat. Return any cooked chicken set aside during the previous step. Stir in 1 tbsp (15 mL) reduced-sodium soy sauce, 1/4 cup (60 mL) lime juice, 30 g scallion dark-green parts, 1/2 cup (16 g) cilantro, and 1/2 cup (12 g) torn basil. Rest for 5 minutes. Stir and divide the complete batch evenly among 6 servings, distributing chicken, edamame and vegetables evenly. There is no additional salt in the base recipe; the curry paste and soy sauce already supply it.
notes: The tofu proposal is replaced with chicken, not simply relabeled: the recipe includes browning, a raw-chicken handling sequence and a 165 F (74 C) endpoint. Edamame stays for extra substance and plant protein. This is tofu-free, not soy-free.

Flavor: cook the curry paste briefly before diluting it, brown the mushrooms, use thin carrot slices, and add lime and fresh herbs off heat. Four cups of broth plus one can of light coconut milk keep the base concentrated without needing multiple cans of coconut milk.

The 4 tbsp (60 g) curry-paste amount assumes a mild supermarket-style paste. A very hot concentrated Thai paste is not a one-for-one substitution: use 2 tbsp (30 g) of that paste initially instead of 4 tbsp, keeping all other quantities unchanged, and expect a different flavor/sodium profile. Do not add an unmeasured spoonful. Check that the chosen paste fits your heat tolerance and the label guidance; some contain shrimp or fish.

Health-conscious design: lean unbrined chicken, edamame, substantial vegetables and measured oil. Use light coconut milk, not coconut cream or a sweetened coconut drink; coconut still contributes saturated fat. Choose the listed broth, curry-paste and soy-sauce sodium levels. No separate sugar or salt is added, but packaged condiments may contain them. This is not a low-sodium certification.

Meal prep: divide into 6 shallow containers and refrigerate at 40 F (4 C) or below within 2 hours, or within 1 hour above 90 F (32 C). Do not cool the full pot on the counter. Use refrigerated portions within 3-4 days. Freeze portions for later days on prep day, leaving expansion room, and plan to use them within 3 months for quality. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

Reheat one portion with 2 tbsp (30 mL) water, stirring so any separated coconut milk recombines. Bring the soup briefly to a rolling boil and verify the chicken and center reach 165 F (74 C). Do not continue boiling once hot. For microwave reheating, cover loosely, stir halfway and check several spots reach 165 F (74 C). Vegetables will soften during storage and freezing; freezer texture has not been kitchen-tested.

Allergens: soy from edamame and soy sauce; conventional soy sauce generally contains wheat. Curry paste may contain shrimp, fish or soy depending on brand. The recipe also contains coconut. Optional brown rice is a separate side, not part of the six-portion base recipe or its shopping quantities.
Developed and reviewed in writing; not yet kitchen-tested. Numerical nutrition estimates are not published because final product labels and a complete calculation have not been verified.
title: Thai Red Curry Chicken, Edamame and Vegetable Soup
